extracted.intended_audience: authors, illustrators, publishers, and librarians interested in the Sibert Medal (children's informational books)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for the Robert F. Sibert Informational Book Medal, the annual American Library Association award for the most distinguished informational book for children. Useful for creators and publishers to determine whether a book qualifies and how the award is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose — "the most distinguished informational book" for children
rubrics_metrics.description: "the most distinguished informational book" for children (quotation from the article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Robert F. Sibert Informational Book Medal is awarded annually to recognize the single most distinguished informational book published in English during the preceding year; the medal is presented by the Association for Library Service to Children (ALSC), a division of the American Library Association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "informational books"
rubrics_metrics.description: "Informational books are defined as those written and illustrated to present, organize, and interpret documentable, factual material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition emphasizes factual, documentable content and includes both writing and illustration as modes of presenting information. The page cites ALSC's terms and criteria for this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre exclusions — poetry and traditional literature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Poetry and traditional literature such as folktales are not eligible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly excludes poetry and traditional literature/folktales from eligibility. The page notes this exclusion while also clarifying that there are no other genre-based restrictions (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: No other restriction on format (reference/nonfiction allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no other restriction, such as reference books or nonfiction books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although poetry and traditional literature are excluded, reference works and nonfiction formats are not barred from consideration; the award focuses on informational quality rather than specific subgenre labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication/location/language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "The book must be published originally or simultaneously in the United States and in English."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible books must be published in English and either originally published in the U.S. or simultaneously published there. Additionally, the award recognizes books published during the preceding year (i.e., annual award cycle).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients — who receives the medal
rubrics_metrics.description: The medal "is awarded annually to the writer and illustrator of the most distinguished informational book published in English during the preceding year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the author (writer) and the illustrator are recognized as recipients when the winning informational book includes distinct contributions from both; ALSC administers the award.
